item.title: "Working Together to Protect Our Neighbors" Public Outreach Meeting — Thu Sep 10, 6:00 PM — Davis Veterans Memorial Center
item.description:
“Working Together to Protect Our Neighbors” Public Outreach Meeting Each year, the City of Davis Police Accountability Commission organizes a community outreach meeting on a local law enforcement topic. Please join us for “Working Together to Protect Our Neighbors,” an event that will explore the local law enforcement response to immigration issues, on Thursday, Sept. 10, from 6-7:30 p.m. at Veterans Memorial Center (203 E. 14th Street). We have three expert speakers for this event:
Michael Gennaco, The OIR Group, City of Davis Independent Police Auditor, will speak about the legal boundaries and accountability expectations governing local law enforcement when federal immigration enforcement occurs in or near our community Todd Henry, City of Davis Police Chief, will speak about the Davis Police can and cannot do in cases of federal immigration enforcement in Davis. item.title: Self Defense Class — Thu Sep 10, 6:00 PM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:
This is a safe, inclusive opportunity to learn self defense from a dedicated group of martial arts practitioners at the Davis Arts Center. If you have ever felt like you would like to learn a little more about how to defend yourself and your loved ones, and would like to get a little fitness training too, please join us! No experience necessary, start any time. We ask for a $10 donation per class, but you can pay whatever you can.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony — Fri Sep 11, 8:30 AM — Fire Station 31
item.description:
9/11 Remembrance Ceremony in Davis
September 11th Remembrance Ceremony Hosted by City of Davis Fire Department Sept. 11, 8:30a Fire Station 31 530 5th Street Information from: City of Davis news alerts The City of Davis Fire Department invites the community to join us on 9/11 at 8:30 a.m. at Fire Station 31 (530 5th Street) for a remembrance ceremony honoring the lives lost on September 11, 2001 and the courage and sacrifice of the first responders who answered the call. This year marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. While a quarter century has passed, we continue to remember the nearly 3,000 people who lost their lives, the families forever changed and the firefighters, law enforcement officers, emergency personnel and everyday people who responded with extraordinary courage. All are welcome to attend and join us as we remember those we lost, honor those who served and reflect on the courage and unity that followed.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Waldorf School's Parent & Child Class — Fri Sep 11, 10:00 AM — Davis Waldorf School
item.description:
The first three years in a child’s life are an amazing time of growth that fill parents and caregivers with awe and wonder. Parent & Child classes are held in a warm and welcoming environment that is carefully arranged for creative play in our Buttercup Preschool room. This program offers the very young child freedom to explore within loving boundaries, and teaches parents/caregivers about Waldorf education’s many benefits. Classes are led by an experienced Early Childhood educator and echo the rhythms of the Waldorf preschool. Additionally, classes offer caregivers a place to connect about child development and parenting techniques. We welcome caregivers of all kinds—parents, grandparents, nannies—to join our sessions!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Live@DCC Free Noon Concert - FluteSong4! — Fri Sep 11, 12:00 PM — Davis Community Church (DCC)
item.description:
Live@DCC 2nd Friday Free noon concerts present FluteSong4 in Concert: An Odyssey Across Borders. Please come enjoy an hour of flute quartet music featuring many composers including Debussy, Elgar, Duke Ellington, and Samuel Coleridge-Taylor! item.description:
Iama Embodied Community What if you gave yourself permission to slow down, breathe, move, and listen to what your body is telling you?
**Healing Movement** is a trauma-informed, embodied spiritual practice that creates space to gently connect with ourselves through movement, breath, music, mindfulness, and reflection.
Together, we’ll explore movement as a way of noticing and moving through the emotions we carry in our bodies—whether that’s grief, anger, fear, shame, joy, or simply the everyday experiences that can be difficult to put into words.
**No dance experience is required.** This is not a dance class, workout, or performance. There is no right way to move. You’re invited to participate at whatever level feels comfortable for you, with an emphasis on choice, gentleness, and listening to your own body.
